entries.t: Krishna Water Board Deadlocks Again in Hyderabad — AP Wants 66%, Telangana Wants 50:50, and the Board Sided With Neither, Ordering Drinking Water First
entries.s: The Krishna River Management Board’s three-member committee met in Hyderabad on Friday for the second time in two weeks and again failed to agree how to split this year’s Krishna water between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — AP wants 66%, Telangana wants a 50:50 split plus 200 TMC, and each side accuses the other of drawing water improperly. With El Niño drought risk cited on all sides, the Board ordered that available water go to drinking-water needs first, not farm irrigation, and told both states to simply follow the 2014 Reorganisation Act until the next meeting, expected in the last week of September. Why this one today: This is not an abstract interstate spat — it lands directly on top of BRS leader KT Rama Rao’s 14 September deadline for the Telangana government to announce a Nagarjuna Sagar Left Canal irrigation-release schedule, on pain of a farmers’ padayatra. A board that just prioritised drinking water over irrigation has made that political deadline much harder for the state government to meet cleanly, and the fight runs straight through canal-command farmland in Nalgonda — exactly the kind of land-value, irrigation-certainty question a plotting developer needs to track.

entries.t: Andhra Pradesh and Telangana failed again to agree on how to split Krishna river water, with drinking water now getting priority over farm irrigation
entries.s: The Krishna River Management Board’s three-member committee met in Hyderabad on Friday, 4 September, to decide how much Krishna water each state gets, and ended in the same deadlock as its last meeting on 24 August. Telangana wants a 50:50 split and has asked for 200 TMC of water citing El Niño-linked drought fears; Andhra Pradesh wants 66% for itself and 34% for Telangana. With no deal, the Board told both states to keep using water strictly under the terms already fixed in the 2014 AP Reorganisation Act, and said it will meet again in the last week of September. Why it matters to you: this fight decides whether canal water reaches farmland on schedule — and BRS leader KTR has already given the government a 14 September deadline over exactly this reservoir, so any land you evaluate in the Nagarjuna Sagar canal command area (Nalgonda, Miryalaguda belt) has its irrigation certainty, and therefore its price, riding on this unresolved dispute.

entries.t: High Court Stops Telangana From Evicting Four Gandipet Landowners Over Musi Riverfront Land, Questions Skipping the Mandatory Social Impact Study
entries.s: The Telangana High Court, hearing a writ petition from four landowners in Dargah Khaliz Khan village, Gandipet mandal, has directed the state government not to dispossess them of roughly 9.08¾ acres for two weeks while it examines their challenge to the land’s acquisition for the 55-km Musi River Development Front project. Justice Kaja Sarath asked the government to file its counter-affidavit within two weeks; the petitioners argue the state used a Section 10A exemption to skip the Social Impact Assessment normally required before large land acquisitions, on land they say sits inside a bio-conservation buffer near the Himayat Sagar reservoir. Why it matters to you: the state has been leaning on this same Section 10A exemption to move faster on land for its mega-projects; if courts start restricting it, government acquisition near ecologically sensitive corridors (including catchment belts like this one) gets slower and more litigation-prone — which cuts both ways for a plotting developer holding or eyeing land in a project-affected zone.

entries.t: A Daughter’s Birthday-Party Speech, a Rs 200-Crore Land Question, and a Cabinet Seat Hanging on a Rakhi
entries.s: Telangana Forest, Environment & Endowments Minister Konda Surekha is one Congress high-command signature away from losing her Cabinet seat and being suspended from the party for six months, after her daughter Konda Sushmitha Patel publicly called Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy “arrogant” and accused his brother’s company of getting government land worth an alleged Rs 200 crore for about Rs 7 crore. A party disciplinary panel has recommended action; the file now sits with a Delhi-based party functionary who is out of the country; and in the meantime, Surekha has tied a ceremonial rakhi to the same Chief Minister and gone right on running her ministry. Why this one today: Telangana real estate itself had a genuinely quiet 24 hours — no big project launch, no policy notification, no rate revision worth a deep dive. But sitting in the middle of this political story is the single largest land-value number in the entire edition: a five-acre government plot that opposition leaders say is worth roughly Rs 200 crore, allotted for about Rs 7 crore to a company with zero employees. For a plotting developer trying to understand how land gets allotted, valued, and fought over in Telangana, that is the highest-stakes, most instructive story on the table today — even though it wears a political costume.

entries.t: A Kompally builder collected money for “Lake View” flats in 2021, never got approval, never broke ground — five years and two penalties later, Telangana’s regulator has ordered every rupee back, with interest
entries.s: On 25 August, TG-RERA ordered Bharathi Builders Pvt Ltd to refund, with 10.7% annual interest, every rupee collected from 12 buyers of “Bharathi’s Lake View Apartments” in Kompally — a project pre-launched in 2021 that never obtained RERA registration, never got HMDA approval, and never broke ground. This is not the builder’s first brush with the regulator: TG-RERA fined it roughly ₹1.18 crore in earlier proceedings, then ₹4.74 crore in March 2026 for the illegal pre-launch sale itself, and formally declared it a “Defaulter Promoter” — barred from registering any new project in the state. Why this one today: today’s other stories are a political party disciplining its own legislator and a housing lottery running on schedule — neither touches how land or apartments actually change hands. This one does, directly: it is a five-year, fully-documented, start-to-finish case study in exactly the failure mode a plotting developer must never repeat — collecting money before registration exists — and in exactly the enforcement tool (TG-RERA’s public Defaulter Promoter list) that now exists to punish it. It is also not an isolated incident: TG-RERA has fined or refunded buyers of at least half a dozen Hyderabad projects in the past month alone, making this the clearest live signal of how seriously the regulator is now being enforced.

entries.s: TG-RERA members Jannu Laxmi Narayana and K Srinivasa Rao ordered Bharathi Builders Pvt Ltd and its associates to refund all money collected from 12 buyers of “Bharathi’s Lake View Apartments” in Kompally, with 10.7% annual interest, within 60 days. Buyers had paid under 2021 pre-launch offers promising possession in 24 months plus a 6-month grace period; no RERA registration was ever obtained, no HMDA approval was secured, and no construction ever began. TG-RERA had already fined the builder roughly ₹1.18 crore in earlier proceedings and ₹4.74 crore in March 2026, declaring it a “Defaulter Promoter” barred from registering fresh projects in the state. Why it matters to you: this is a full, checkable case study of the exact mistake to never make as a developer, and the exact check every buyer should run before paying you — search TG-RERA’s Defaulter Promoter list yourself, on any project, before any money changes hands.

Why it matters to you: not a land story, but AIMIM holds seats in the Legislative Council that vote on any bill needing Upper House passage — including whatever land-pooling legislation reaches the House this session — so a forced vacancy here is a small but real shift in Council arithmetic right before the 7 September Assembly session.

entries.t: Telangana just reopened registration on 1,500 frozen Paigah acres — in the same corridor, the same week, a plot next door sold for ₹269 crore an acre
entries.s: On 28 August, Telangana’s Revenue Minister announced the government will let owners register property on roughly 1,500 acres of long-disputed Paigah land — CS-14 and CS-7, frozen under Section 22A for a 1958 ownership dispute that’s still in court — with a catch: the deed itself will say your title is conditional on how the Supreme Court and High Court eventually rule. The same CS-7 parcel covers Miyapur and Raidurg — the exact corridor where, the same week, a TGIIC auction plot sold for a record ₹269 crore an acre. Why this one today: Everything else in today’s edition is either a market data point (the Raidurg auction itself) or politics that touches land only indirectly. This story is different: it is a government instrument that directly changes whether specific parcels in Hafeezpet, Kondapur, Hydernagar, Hasmatpet, Malkajgiri, Miyapur and Raidurg — several of them live JD corridors — can be registered at all. For a plotting developer, a registrability switch flipping on thousands of frozen units is a bigger structural event than any single auction price, however record-breaking. It also arrives as the direct sequel to the Section 22A crisis your Concept Library has been tracking for weeks — this is the government’s first concrete fix, and it comes with a caveat (“conditional”) that is itself the whole story.

entries.t: Hyderabad breaks its own land-price record again — Raidurg plot sells for ₹269 crore an acre, the third record this year
entries.s: TGIIC auctioned Plot P2, a 5.38-acre parcel in Knowledge City, Raidurg, on Friday, fetching ₹1,447.22 crore — a record ₹269 crore per acre and a 52.3% premium over the ₹175-crore reserve. Vamsiram Builders won the bid. It comes exactly a week after neighbouring Plot P1 sold for ₹264 crore per acre; together the two plots have fetched TGIIC ₹2,833.22 crore from 10.63 acres. Why it matters to you: this is now the third Hyderabad land-price record broken in this corridor within a year (₹177cr in Oct 2025, ₹237cr in May 2026, now ₹269cr) — the clearest, most-corroborated benchmark going for what institutional buyers will pay for clean-titled Raidurg/Knowledge City land, useful the next time you’re valuing collateral or negotiating a JD share anywhere near this corridor.

entries.t: Telangana to allow “conditional” registration on 1,500 acres of frozen Paigah land in Hafeezpet, Kondapur, Miyapur and Raidurg
entries.s: Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said the government will remove CS-14 and CS-7 Paigah-estate land — frozen under Section 22A since a 1958 ownership dispute — from the prohibited list, allowing “conditional” registrations whose deeds will state ownership remains subject to pending Supreme Court and High Court rulings. The move could regularise thousands of existing homes across Hafeezpet, Kondapur, Hydernagar, Hasmatpet, Malkajgiri, Miyapur and Raidurg, unlocking an estimated ₹1,000 crore in registration revenue. Implementation will be case-by-case, not a blanket release. Why it matters to you: if you deal in any of these named localities, go check whether your survey number sits inside CS-14 or CS-7 — this can flip a parcel from unregistrable to transactable overnight, but a “conditional” deed carries real, disclosed litigation risk you must underwrite, not a clean title.

entries.t: How two laws, changed on one afternoon, quietly opened the door to selling off Lalbagh
entries.s: On 24 August 2026, Karnataka’s legislature passed two amendments in a single sitting: one lets the government sell, lease or mortgage up to 5% of any government park’s land for “public infrastructure,” the other retroactively legalises transport-project decisions taken before the rules that were meant to govern them existed. Both changes land squarely on Lalbagh, the 240-acre botanical garden that stands in the path of a planned ₹22,267-crore tunnel road — and for which Adani Group, days after meeting the Chief Minister, has just emerged as lowest bidder. Why this one today: Nothing else in today’s edition touches Hyderabad plotting directly — this is a Bengaluru story, not a Telangana one. It still takes the flagship slot because of what it is underneath the geography: a fresh, live, working precedent for how a state legislature can carve a legal exemption into a protected-land law specifically to unlock one parcel for one project. The mechanic being used here — “alienation” of a small percentage of protected land, dressed as a public-infrastructure carve-out — is the exact same mechanic that governs FTL (Full Tank Level) and buffer-zone land around Hyderabad’s lakes, including the ongoing Musi riverfront redevelopment. On the weighting Vivek uses every day — direct Hyderabad plotting impact, then Telangana land policy, then politics that moves land or money — this story would normally rank third. It earns the top slot today because it is the single most transferable land-law lesson in the whole edition: watch what happens to Lalbagh, and you are watching a preview of what a similar carve-out bill would look like if it ever reached Telangana’s FTL or buffer-zone rules.

entries.t: Greater Bengaluru Authority starts bulldozing dirty vacant plots itself — and will bill owners through their property tax.
entries.s: Only about 20% of Bengaluru’s vacant plot owners cleaned up their own sites even after the GBA’s deadline was extended from 15 August to 22 August. Why it matters to you: if you or your clients are sitting on unbuilt/vacant plots anywhere in GBA limits, an uncleaned site is no longer just an eyesore — it is now a guaranteed line item on next year’s tax notice, with repeat offenders facing separate fines of ₹25,000 to ₹1 lakh.

entries.t: Citizens accuse Karnataka of quietly rewriting park and transport laws to clear the path for the Adani-linked tunnel road under Lalbagh.
entries.s: On 24 August the Karnataka legislature passed amendments to two laws on the same day — the Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975 (allowing up to 5% of any park to be alienated for public infrastructure) and the BMLTA Act, 2022 (giving retrospective legal cover to transport-project decisions taken before its rules were notified). By 27–28 August, over 200 citizen groups, environmentalists and BJP MP Tejasvi Surya were publicly demanding the Governor return the Parks Bill, pointing out this happened just a day after Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani met CM D K Shivakumar — and Adani has since emerged as the lowest bidder for the ₹22,267-crore Hebbal–Silk Board tunnel road, which needs nearly 5 acres of Lalbagh. Why it matters to you: watch this precedent closely — a legal mechanism that lets government convert “protected” green/public land into usable project land for infrastructure could eventually be extended to other protected or reserved categories of land that plotting developers deal with.

entries.t: One crore acres, one verbal instruction at a time: how Telangana’s land registry broke, and why the fix keeps almost working
entries.s: The Section 22A prohibited-property crisis, taken apart from zero: why a land-records migration project turned into a statewide freeze, why the fix keeps being partial, why two districts erupted in sit-ins this week, and what a government correcting legal records through verbal instructions rather than written rules means for every deal you evaluate in Telangana right now. Why this one today: it is the single biggest, most actively escalating land-policy story in this edition — it touches every district, it is a live governance-process failure (not just a data backlog), and it is the exact kind of systemic risk that has to be priced into every acquisition you make until the state actually finishes fixing it.

entries.t: The Section 22A crisis enters its fourth week — and now two districts are staging sit-ins
entries.s: The Section 22A prohibited-property list, which had vanished from Telangana’s Bhu Bharati portal weeks ago, reappeared on the Registration & Stamps Department’s website on Tuesday — but the Wakf and Endowments categories still return only “Prohibition data is under review.” The same day, landowners staged sit-in protests in Karimnagar and Vikarabad districts demanding their properties be struck off the list, and a Telugu-language report citing revenue officials said the government has been correcting entries through verbal instructions rather than published guidelines — leaving field officers without a written rulebook to act on. Separately reported figures put roughly 76,000 acres locked up in Jangaon and Hanumakonda districts alone, and the statewide prohibited-list total above one crore acres. Why it matters to you: this is no longer a data-entry backlog you can wait out — it is now a governance-process problem (oral instructions, not written rules) that is visibly spreading to new districts. Any parcel you are evaluating anywhere in Telangana, not just Hyderabad-adjacent areas, needs an independent 22A check before you advance money, because the list itself is being edited off the record.
entries.src: Sources: Deccan Chronicle, The Hans India & Namasthe Telangana (BRS-aligned — bias flagged below) · published 26–27 Aug 2026 (Wed–Thu, rolling coverage)

entries.t: TG-RERA unblocks registration for 24 stuck Jaya Diamonds flat buyers, gives the promoter 60 days
entries.s: The Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority relaxed its earlier order on the stalled Jaya Diamonds residential project in Nizampet/Pragathi Nagar, permitting the jurisdictional Sub-Registrar to register sale deeds for 24 named flat buyers once title, identity and legal compliance are verified. The project’s promoter has been given 60 days to complete execution and registration of those deeds and must file a compliance report with TG-RERA’s Monitoring Committee. In February 2026, TG-RERA had already allowed the project’s homebuyers’ association to take over and finish construction itself under Section 8 of the RERA Act, after the original developer failed to deliver. Why it matters to you: this is what RERA enforcement actually looks like when it works for the buyer — a stalled project doesn’t just get you a compensation order on paper, it can get your specific flat’s registration unblocked even while construction disputes continue elsewhere in the same project. If you ever broker, finance or advise on a stalled project, TG-RERA’s Section 8 takeover-plus-partial-registration route is the template to know.

The BRS-aligned outlet reporting this frames it as part of a wider pattern of HYDRAA using excavators to demolish self-built homes along the same corridor, where the agency had already cleared illegal shops and temporary sheds earlier this month after prior notices. Why it matters to you: single-source, politically-aligned reporting on a HYDRAA action is exactly the kind of story where the other side (HYDRAA’s own justification, any notice history on this specific plot) isn’t in this account at all — but the underlying pattern (HYDRAA enforcement activity on the Miyapur–Gandi Maisamma corridor) is real and recurring, and it matters if you or your clients hold anything near it.

At a separate gathering of 22A-affected families in KPHB Colony, he accused Chief Minister Revanth Reddy of running a “land-centric,” not “people-centric,” government, alleging the state had sold roughly ₹30,000 crore of government land in a short period while ordinary landowners were harassed by the same list. Why it matters to you: whether or not you credit BRS’s specific numbers, this tells you the 22A crisis has become the state’s central opposition attack line — which gives the government strong political incentive to actually finish fixing it soon, and equally strong incentive to keep managing it quietly rather than admit fault publicly. entries.t: The Konda Surekha fallout, day two: the CM declines comment, and her husband meets the Deputy CM amid backchannel speculation
entries.s: A day after TPCC’s own disciplinary committee recommended sacking Forest Minister Konda Surekha from the Cabinet, CM Revanth Reddy declined to comment publicly on Wednesday, telling Ministers, MLAs, MLCs and MPs gathered at the Secretariat that the Congress high command’s decision would be final and urging them to stop commenting in the media until it arrives. The same day, senior Congress leader Konda Murali — Surekha’s husband — met Deputy CM Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka at Praja Bhavan alongside Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajagopal Reddy and Irrigation Minister Uttam Kumar Reddy; both Murali and Rajagopal Reddy told reporters the meeting was only about pending local-constituency bills, though the timing — immediately after the disciplinary report — triggered speculation about backchannel efforts on Surekha’s behalf. Why it matters to you: the decision on whether Surekha keeps her Cabinet seat sits with the AICC high command in Delhi now, not in Hyderabad — and until it lands, the Endowments & Forest portfolio she holds (which administers land bordering exactly the categories you track) stays in political limbo. Watch who inherits it if she goes.

He specifically criticised Revanth’s plan to meet New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, describing him as a “pro-Pakistan figure” critical of India, and said the US leg’s itinerary was found inappropriate for a sitting Chief Minister. Why it matters to you: a CM this consumed by a Centre-state word war over a foreign trip is a CM whose bandwidth for actually drafting and pushing the land-pooling and CURE Bills through the 7 September session keeps getting diverted — track what officials are drafting quietly, not just what leaders say at podiums.

entries.t: Cyberabad's demolition drive widens: 17 more illegal buildings razed overnight, 54 more flagged citywide

entries.s: Comptroller and Auditor General figures show Telangana's revenue deficit reached ₹19,266.83 crore over April–July, with the fiscal deficit already at 57.7% of the full-year target (₹33,729.98 crore of a ₹58,458.71 crore annual estimate). Revenue receipts of ₹59,642.62 crore were just 24.72% of the year's ₹2.41 lakh crore target, while revenue expenditure of ₹78,909.45 crore had already used up 33.66% of its ₹2.34 lakh crore allocation — spending is outrunning collections early in the year. Why it matters to you: this is the fiscal backdrop behind almost every land story this week — HMDA's aggressive e-auction calendar, the push for land pooling over cash acquisition, TDR instead of compensation cheques. A government this short on cash has every incentive to monetise land fast, which affects both supply and pricing in auctioned pockets.

entries.t: Two days after the Gachibowli building collapse killed two workers, Cyberabad flags 38 illegal buildings and demolishes nine
entries.s: Two days after an illegal seven-storey building under construction on a 50-square-yard Anjaiah Nagar (Gachibowli) plot collapsed and killed two migrant workers, Cyberabad Municipal Corporation Commissioner G. Srijana ordered a city-wide sweep for unauthorised under-construction buildings. Teams flagged 38 such buildings, served notices on 28, seized one, and demolished nine — while HYDRAA resumed demolishing a second structurally damaged building at the original site using its high-reach "Bahubali" machine. Why it matters to you: the enforcement rule used here is exactly the one that governs small plots — under 75 sq. yards, anything over 7 metres (roughly ground+1) needs full sanction, and this crackdown shows officials are actively hunting for exactly that violation right now across Cyberabad, not just at the collapse site.

entries.t: Assembly session confirmed for 7 September — CM tells MLAs to speed up land acquisition, with the CURE and Land Pooling Bills expected on the floor
entries.s: CM A. Revanth Reddy told MLAs at a Secretariat meeting that the Legislative Assembly's monsoon session will begin on 7 September, and directed them to expedite pending land acquisition for irrigation projects, promising funds for acquisition, Relief & Rehabilitation and forest clearances. The statewide Land Pooling Bill (landowners reportedly getting back 60% of developed plots, HMDA/TGIIC keeping 40%) and the CURE Bill replacing the GHMC Act are both expected to come up in that session. Why it matters to you: 7 September is now the date to actually watch for the land-pooling framework's fine print — ratios, eligibility, who administers it — rather than the vaguer "coming soon" you've heard so far.

entries.t: Back in Hyderabad, Revanth Reddy calls the US-trip denial "an insult to Telangana," accuses the Centre of political bias — but ducks the Konda Surekha question
entries.s: At a press conference at the Secretariat, CM A. Revanth Reddy said the Ministry of External Affairs's denial of political clearance for the US leg of his tour was "not a denial to Revanth Reddy but a disrespect to the people of Telangana," asking why the UK leg was cleared but not the US one if nothing political was involved. He called it "Gujarat supremacy" and demanded PM Modi explain personally, while confirming the Telangana Global Summit 2026 for 8–9 December. Asked about Konda Surekha, he declined comment, saying the party disciplinary process must run its course. Why it matters to you: the CM is now fully engaged domestically — watch whether that translates into actual movement on the Konda Surekha Cabinet question and the pending land bills, rather than another round of Centre-state sparring.

entries.t: Government hits back on Section 22A: Revenue Minister says 98% of registrations already cleared, forms a 15-day fast-track committee for Hyderabad's four districts
entries.s: Answering BRS's Harish Rao, Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said claims that "lakhs of acres" were wrongly frozen under Section 22A were a "misleading Opposition campaign," and that 98% of registrations sought under the provision have already been cleared. Of 980 distinct grievance-line complaints (547 agricultural, 433 non-agricultural) and over 300 relaxation requests, only 12–13 were rejected. He announced a high-level committee — the Revenue Principal Secretary, the IG of Registration and Stamps, and district officials from Hyderabad, Rangareddy, Sangareddy and Medchal-Malkajgiri — to review genuine cases daily for 15 days, with fees refunded within a week and grievances resolved in 24–36 hours. Why it matters to you: this is the most actionable 22A news since the crisis began — a named 15-day window (ending roughly 8 September) and a specific toll-free/committee process across the four districts that cover almost all of metro Hyderabad's plotting activity. If you have a frozen survey number, this is the process to actually use.
entries.src: Sources: Siasat, NTV Telugu, NewsMeter & Telangana Tribune · published 24 Aug 2026 (Monday, Secretariat press conference)

entries.t: Report: Congress high command gives Konda Surekha a resign-by-this-evening ultimatum; minister refuses
entries.s: The Hans India reports the Congress high command asked Endowments & Forest Minister Konda Surekha, via a senior minister from erstwhile Nalgonda district, to resign by Tuesday (today) evening or face dismissal — and that she has refused, maintaining she made no remarks against the CM or party. This follows her 23 August meeting with AICC chief Kharge, who reportedly told her to settle the matter with the TPCC rather than the high command. Why it matters to you: unconfirmed by a second outlet, so treat as a rumour with a deadline rather than fact — but if her Endowments & Forest portfolio does change hands today, note who replaces her, since that person will administer land bordering exactly the categories you need to watch.

entries.t: Karnataka Legislature passes ₹7,042.69-crore supplementary budget with ₹1,000 crore earmarked for Bengaluru road infrastructure, then adjourns sine die three days early
entries.s: Amid the Opposition's protest over Minister B. Nagendra (see Karnataka Politics), the Karnataka Legislature passed a first-instalment supplementary budget of ₹7,042.69 crore (₹4,324.35 crore revenue, ₹2,718.35 crore capital) before Speaker G.S. Patil adjourned the Monsoon Session sine die — three days ahead of its scheduled 27 August finish. The capital allocation includes ₹1,000 crore earmarked for Bengaluru road development. The Government Parks (Preservation) Amendment Bill, Cabinet-cleared on 21–22 August to allow up to 5% of any park to be alienated for infrastructure, was reported by some outlets as passed the same day — we could not independently confirm Assembly passage of that specific bill , so treat its status as still "Cabinet-cleared, not yet law" until confirmed. Why it matters to you: ₹1,000 crore for Bengaluru roads is a real, funded infrastructure line — worth tracking which corridors it targets, since road spending is one of the more reliable early signals of where land values move next. The park-land bill is not yet law, whatever some reports implied — don't act on it as settled.
entries.src: Sources: countryandpolitics.in, The Hans India & ANI · published 24 Aug 2026

entries.t: The siege happened: police detain Vijayendra, Ashoka and CT Ravi at Vidhana Soudha; Assembly then adjourned sine die, three days early, with Nagendra still in his job
entries.s: The BJP-JD(S) march from Freedom Park to Vidhana Soudha went ahead at 9:30 AM on 24 August as announced. Police blocked all gates and pre-emptively detained BJP state president B.Y. Vijayendra, Leader of the Opposition R. Ashoka and senior leader CT Ravi, along with many cadre. Ashoka accused police of rough handling and announced an indefinite day-and-night Assembly dharna until Minister B. Nagendra resigns over the Valmiki Corporation scam — but the Speaker adjourned the session sine die that same day, three days ahead of schedule, effectively ending the sitting the Opposition had vowed to occupy. BJP leaders then marched to Raj Bhavan and petitioned Governor Thawarchand Gehlot to seek an explanation from CM D.K. Shivakumar. Nagendra has not resigned. Why it matters to you: same lesson as yesterday, now with a harder edge — the government let the whole Assembly session end early rather than remove one minister. When an institution will sacrifice its own legislative calendar to protect a person, that person (or whoever controls what he controls) is more important to the power structure than the session itself.
entries.src: Sources: ANI (multiple wires, 10:08 AM–2:50 PM IST), Deccan Herald, The Statesman, The Week & Deccan Chronicle · published 24 Aug 2026

entries.t: Karnataka's first SIR draft electoral roll cuts 1.07 crore names — nearly half of Bengaluru's voter list flagged for review
entries.s: Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) draft electoral roll shows 4.47 crore voters, down from 5.54 crore — 1.07 crore names (about 19%) moved to an "Absent/Shifted/Dead/Duplicate/Other" category pending verification. In Bengaluru alone, 46.88 lakh of 1.03 crore voters (45%) are flagged, split almost evenly between BJP-held and Congress-held seats. Claims and objections run 24 August–23 September; the final roll is due 27 October. Why it matters to you: not a land story directly, but a reminder of how fast a "provisional" government list — voter roll today, survey number tomorrow — can knock someone off a register pending paperwork. The same discipline (check, don't assume) applies to both.
entries.src: Sources: Siasat, Deccan Herald & Scroll.in · published 24 Aug 2026

entries.t: Revanth Reddy flies home from London after the Centre blocks his US leg on a "political" ground — and promises to "speak in Hyderabad"
entries.s: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy cut short his "Telangana Rising" tour and returned to Hyderabad from London on 23 August, after the Ministry of External Affairs cleared the UK leg but denied political clearance for the US leg, which the MEA said involved a "planned programme not appropriate to the office held." Revanth called the denial politically motivated and said he would explain the matter in detail at a press conference once back in Hyderabad. He thanked AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge for his backing and, rather than cancel outright, ordered the official delegation to continue to the US to sign MoUs with Harvard, MIT, Northeastern and Virginia Tech in his absence. Why it matters to you: the CM is now physically back in Hyderabad — the trigger multiple reports said could unlock decisions on the Konda Surekha Cabinet question and other pending matters. Watch what he actually does in the next few days, not what the tour headlines promised: the investment MoUs are intent, not funded projects.

entries.t: Harish Rao threatens to stall the Assembly and gherao the Secretariat over Section 22A — names three colonies he wants struck off the freeze list
entries.s: BRS deputy floor leader T. Harish Rao escalated the Section 22A land-freeze fight at a party meeting in Boduppal supporting affected residents, warning that BRS would stall the coming Assembly session and lay siege to ("gherao") the Secretariat if the Congress government does not withdraw what he called unjust prohibitory listings. He specifically demanded that Tirumala Meadows, Lakshmi Ganapathi and Hemanagar colonies be removed from the Section 22A restricted list, alleging fully registered houses were being placed under the freeze to enable illegal collections, and that middle-class families could no longer get bank loans or sell their properties as a result. Why it matters to you: this is the exact mechanism that can freeze a plot mid-deal — a registered, patta property swept onto the 22A list. Note the named colonies (all Boduppal/Medchal-Malkajgiri side) as elevated-risk zones, and treat "it's registered" as necessary but not sufficient until you've personally checked the live 22A list for the survey number.

entries.t: Konda Surekha flies to Bengaluru to meet Kharge — who tells her to settle the rift with the state unit, not the high command
entries.s: Endowments & Forest Minister Konda Surekha met AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge in Bengaluru (reportedly for about 15 minutes) to brief him on the Congress rift caused by her daughter Konda Sushmita's remarks against CM Revanth Reddy. Surekha maintained that neither she nor her daughter had criticised the party or the Gandhi family and alleged a conspiracy targeting her family. Kharge reportedly expressed displeasure, cautioned her against remarks that hurt party interests, and told her to resolve it with the TPCC. No formal Cabinet decision on her position has been reported. Why it matters to you: her portfolio covers Endowments & Forest land — two of the trickiest boundary categories a plotting developer can run into. A reshuffle here is worth tracking, but the takeaway today is the political grammar: going over the state unit's head to the high command got her sent right back down to the state unit.
entries.src: Sources: The Hans India & NTV Telugu · published 23 Aug 2026 (Sunday; exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: KTR sets a week-long BRS offensive from Sept 2, timed to the Congress government's 1,000th day: "not one promise fully kept"
entries.s: BRS Working President K.T. Rama Rao (KTR) announced a statewide week-long campaign starting 2 September, timed to the Congress government completing 1,000 days in office, to spotlight what BRS calls its "betrayal" of election promises. KTR said Congress made 420 promises, 13 declarations and six guarantees claiming implementation within 100 days, but had "not fully fulfilled even a single promise" after 1,000 days. He directed cadres to hand out "Baaki Cards" (pending-dues cards) listing unfulfilled welfare commitments to each social group. Why it matters to you: a milestone-timed opposition campaign is a signal, not noise — it tells you which promises the government will feel most pressure to be seen delivering. Anything land- or housing-linked (2BHK schemes, plot regularisation, compensation) tends to get pushed hardest in exactly these anniversary windows.
entries.src: Sources: ANI & Siasat · published 24 Aug 2026 (ANI wire timestamped ~2:44 AM IST)

entries.t: BJP and JD(S) announce a siege of Vidhana Soudha this morning over the Valmiki Corporation scam — demanding Minister Nagendra's removal
entries.s: Karnataka Leader of the Opposition R. Ashoka announced that the BJP, with ally JD(S), would march from Freedom Park and lay siege to Vidhana Soudha at 9:30 AM on Monday, 24 August, demanding the removal of Planning & Statistics Minister B. Nagendra over the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam. Ashoka said an initial ₹89 crore was illegally transferred from the corporation's Union Bank account to various accounts, with the overall alleged diversion later pegged at about ₹187 crore — money he claimed was used to fund Congress campaigns. He said JD(S) chief H.D. Kumaraswamy backed continuing the agitation for another week, and that the BJP had compiled details of 35 cases against Nagendra spanning mining and the Valmiki Corporation. Why it matters to you: this is the same pattern as yesterday's story — the government gave Nagendra an extra portfolio rather than remove him. The lesson for a developer is institutional: watch what happens to a minister who controls large discretionary funds under fire — a government that digs in is telling you where real power sits, which is what actually governs how discretionary land and money get allotted.
entries.src: Sources: ANI, Siasat, Deccan Chronicle & The Hans India · published 23 Aug 2026 (ANI wire timestamped ~12:43 PM IST); the siege itself is scheduled for 9:30 AM 24 Aug — after press time

entries.t: BJP chief Vijayendra vows to fight Karnataka's park-land bill: a "systematic conspiracy" to take over protected green space
entries.s: Karnataka BJP president B.Y. Vijayendra said the party would "make every possible effort to prevent" the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Amendment Bill, calling it "a systematic conspiracy to take over government parks reserved for environmental protection, public health safeguards and other public uses." The bill, cleared by Cabinet on 21–22 August, would let up to 5% of any government park or garden be alienated — sold, leased, gifted, exchanged or mortgaged — for public infrastructure. Critics tie it to the roughly ₹17,770-crore Hebbal–Silk Board tunnel road, which reportedly needs about six acres of Lalbagh temporarily and one acre permanently. Why it matters to you: yesterday you learned the bill exists; today's lesson is that "Cabinet cleared" is only step one — it still needs Assembly passage, Council, and the Governor's assent, and an organised opposition can slow or reshape it at each stage. Never treat a protected-land carve-out as done until it's notified.
entries.src: Sources: The Federal & ANI wire (syndicated) · published 23 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: TPCC panel finds Konda Surekha's daughter "crossed the limits" — but defers action; minister counter-complains against her own party's rebel MLAs
entries.s: Telangana's TPCC Disciplinary Committee, chaired by Lok Sabha MP Mallu Ravi, met for over three hours at Gandhi Bhavan to review showcause replies from Minister Konda Surekha and senior leader G. Chinna Reddy. It informally concluded that Surekha's daughter Konda Sushmita had "crossed the limits" attacking CM Revanth Reddy, and that Surekha herself was at fault for not condemning the remarks — but deferred any formal decision, saying it will meet again. Surekha separately wrote to Mallu Ravi asking the committee to instead investigate the 20+ Congress MLAs demanding her sacking, and whether outside forces are trying to influence its judgment. Why it matters to you: CM Revanth Reddy returns to Hyderabad from London around today, and reports suggest he may take "crucial decisions" on Surekha's Cabinet position soon after — any reshuffle of the Endowments & Forest portfolio is worth tracking if you deal near forest or endowment land boundaries.

entries.t: Revanth pitches Cambridge and London for a Hyderabad "knowledge hub" — but an Oxford meeting ignites a fresh BJP "anti-national" row, and BRS alleges a hawala-linked MoU tied to the CM's brother
entries.s: Telangana's "Telangana Rising" delegation, still in London, met academic teams from Cambridge and the University of London on Saturday to pitch Hyderabad as a future "global knowledge hub"; Cambridge Judge Business School professors Jaideep Prabhu and Venkata Serish Gandikota reportedly expressed interest, and University of London officials discussed a possible Hyderabad campus. But an earlier Oxford meeting with professors Maya Tudor and Faisal Devji — both known for writing critical of Indian democracy and nationalism — became a political flashpoint, with BJP leaders publicly slamming Revanth for meeting figures they call "anti-India." Separately, BRS's Manne Krishank called the Centre's US-leg denial a "diplomatic embarrassment" and asked "is this some sort of hawala business?", alleging an earlier ₹1,000-crore MoU the CM signed in the US involved "Swachh Bio," a new firm owned by his brother Anumula Jagadishwar Reddy. Why it matters to you: a reminder that a state's glossy MoU-tour announcements are marketing, not commitments — MoUs with Harvard, MIT and Cambridge are still just intent until they clear every layer of scrutiny and actually get funded and built.

entries.t: GO 97 protests, round two: Technical Education Commissioner holds fresh talks with polytechnic students — they leave unsatisfied
entries.s: Commissioner of Technical Education A. Sridevasena held talks with polytechnic student representatives over GO 97's plan to fold polytechnics into the new Young India Skill University. Students left the meeting dissatisfied, still demanding the order be withdrawn entirely over fears of fee hikes and a devalued diploma. Why it matters to you: a second round of talks without resolution usually means the underlying order stands — worth remembering that a Government Order, once issued, is genuinely hard to reverse even under sustained protest.

entries.t: Karnataka Cabinet clears a bill to let government carve up to 5% of any park or garden — Cubbon Park and Lalbagh included — for infrastructure projects
entries.s: The Karnataka Cabinet approved a Bill amending the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, to allow up to 5% of any government park or garden's total area to be "alienated" — sold, leased, gifted, exchanged or mortgaged — for public infrastructure or utility projects, restricted to government departments, statutory authorities and local bodies. A high-level committee headed by an Additional Chief Secretary-rank officer will vet which land qualifies. BJP state president B.Y. Vijayendra called it "detrimental to the environment," and MP Tejasvi Surya said "parks are not real-estate assets," alleging the bill exists to route around a pending court challenge to the Hebbal–Silk Board tunnel road project (bid leader: Adani Group) on Parks Act grounds. Why it matters to you: watch this as a precedent — a government rewriting a protective land-use law specifically to unlock infrastructure land under litigation pressure is exactly the kind of move that can also touch forest, endowment or buffer-zone land near a Hyderabad JD site someday.
entries.src: Sources: Business Standard, The Federal & ANI (Tejasvi Surya reaction) · Cabinet clearance 21 Aug 2026; Surya's reaction published in the early hours of 23 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not otherwise stated)

entries.t: Amid resignation demands, Karnataka hands Minister Nagendra an ADDITIONAL charge — the Kalyana Karnataka development secretariat
entries.s: While BJP and JD(S) continue demanding B. Nagendra's resignation over the Valmiki Corporation scam, the Shivakumar-led government gave him an additional charge on top of his Planning & Statistics portfolio: the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Secretariat, which administers the Article 371J special-development fund for the state's northeastern region. BJP called it politically provocative timing. Why it matters to you: a government doubling down on an accused minister, rather than removing him, is the clearest possible signal of where real power actually sits — a pattern to recognise anywhere a minister controls large discretionary development funds.
entries.src: Sources: Asianet Suvarna News, TV9 Kannada & Public TV Kannada · published 22 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Hyderabad's highest-ever government land sale: a Raidurg plot fetches ₹264 crore an acre
entries.s: TGIIC e-auctioned Plot P1, a 5.25-acre parcel in Raidurg, via the MSTC e-auction platform with JLL as transaction advisor. Against a ₹175-crore/acre reserve, bidding closed at ₹264 crore/acre — a 50.9% premium — for a total of ₹1,386 crore, won by MSN Realty. It beats TGIIC's own May 2026 Raidurg sale (₹237 crore/acre) by about 11%, and tops the previous city benchmark from HMDA's Kokapet/Neopolis auctions (~₹151 crore/acre). Why it matters to you: a clean, competitively-bid government auction price is the hardest number to argue with — ₹264 crore/acre is now the reference figure for IT-corridor land anywhere near Raidurg, useful leverage (or a reality check) the next time a JD partner quotes you a per-acre number in a comparable belt.
entries.src: Sources: Siasat , The Hans India & Deccan Chronicle · published 21 Aug 2026, 8:12 PM IST

entries.t: TG-RERA orders ₹42.2-lakh refund to Hyderabad plot buyers after the seller's cheques bounced
entries.s: TG-RERA ordered Trishakti Homes Consultancy to refund ₹42.2 lakh plus 10.7% interest (running from 7 June 2022) to buyers who had booked two plots in "Sree Rugveda Brundavanam Hills" in 2022, later cancelled, and were part-refunded before the rest bounced. The order finds the firm — a registered agent, not the builder — liable under Section 10 of the RERA Act for marketing an unregistered project. Why it matters to you: RERA can hold the selling agent personally liable, not just the builder — always verify a project's own RERA registration number before booking or accepting it into a JD.
entries.src: Source: Siasat · published 21 Aug 2026, 1:00 PM IST

entries.t: Section 22A fallout, day 4: employee unions reject the blame, helpline logs 400 complaints in 3 days
entries.s: Revenue department employee associations publicly pushed back on ministers pinning the prohibited-list crisis on "officials," calling it a policy failure. The state's toll-free 22A helpline logged 400 calls in its first three days — 116 on 20 August alone — with Rangareddy (23), Medchal-Malkajgiri (17), and Sangareddy & Siddipet (10 each) the top-complaint districts. Why it matters to you: the district breakdown is real diligence data — Rangareddy and Medchal-Malkajgiri are exactly the fast-growing plotting belts, so treat land there as higher 22A-risk until you've personally checked the live list.

entries.t: Centre denies political clearance for Revanth's US leg; CM sends the Telangana Rising delegation on anyway
entries.s: After CM Revanth Reddy's delegation reached London on his 10-day UK-US "Telangana Rising" investment tour, the Ministry of External Affairs cleared only the UK leg — the US leg was denied. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the proposed US programme "was not appropriate to the office held." Revanth called the decision political, said he'd return to Hyderabad from London around 23 August, but directed the official delegation to proceed to the US anyway to sign MoUs with Harvard, MIT, Northeastern and Virginia Tech. Telangana BJP chief N. Ramchander Rao denied any "conspiracy." Why it matters to you: Centre-state friction can slow or reshape a state's investment pitch overnight — a reminder to price land on approvals actually cleared, not on a state government's travel-brochure ambitions.

entries.t: Congress revolt: 20+ MLAs demand Konda Surekha's dismissal after she refuses to disown her daughter's attack on the CM
entries.s: After Minister Konda Surekha's written reply to the TPCC Disciplinary Committee called it a breach of "natural justice" to hold her responsible for daughter Konda Sushmita's attack on CM Revanth Reddy, over 20 Congress MLAs — led by Chief Whip Beerla Ilaiah and MLA Vemula Veeresham — held a press conference demanding her sacking from Cabinet and suspension from the party. AICC in-charge Meenakshi Natarajan sought a formal report; TPCC Disciplinary Committee chief Mallu Ravi warned that crossing the party's "Lakshman Rekha" invites action. Why it matters to you: the fastest-moving thread in the ₹200-crore-vs-₹7-crore Raviryal land-allotment story to watch — an internal Congress revolt could push this land-allotment allegation against the CM's brother into a far bigger story.
entries.src: Sources: Deccan Chronicle, The Hans India & ANI · published 21 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

Separately, BRS's KTR and K. Kavitha invoked a 19 August Mahabubabad incident — a police inspector filmed grabbing a protesting student by the throat — to ask why Rahul Gandhi stays silent on "Congress police brutality" in Telangana. Why it matters to you: a reminder that a single state Government Order can restructure an entire institutional category overnight — the same sweeping-order power that created the Section 22A mess.

BRS's KTR called the government "incompetent" on the finding. Why it matters to you: a state already 57.7% through its annual borrowing room in a third of the year has less headroom to fund the roads and ring roads that move land prices.

entries.t: Karnataka Assembly passes a new Apartment Ownership law — and lets civic bodies seize neglected private roads for free
entries.s: Passed without discussion amid Assembly disruption, the Karnataka Apartment (Ownership and Management) Bill, 2026 replaces two 50-year-old laws for projects over 8 units: it mandates one registered RWA per project, sets a 75%-owner-consent threshold for redevelopment (dissenters bought out at 2x market value), requires 5-yearly structural safety audits for buildings over 30 years old, and obliges builders to fund maintenance on unsold flats. Two companion municipal bills let commissioners take over a dilapidated private layout road judged a safety risk and declare it public — with no compensation to its owner. Why it matters to you: any Bengaluru apartment redevelopment or JD now runs on a concrete 75%-consent-plus-2x-buyout formula — and a private access road inside a layout you thought was an asset can now be taken for free.

entries.t: Karnataka Assembly disrupted for a 5th day; BJP MLAs force their way in, Congress blocks its own Kharge resolution in retaliation
entries.s: BJP MLAs in black T-shirts, led by state chief B.Y. Vijayendra and LoP R. Ashoka, marched from the Valmiki statue to Vidhana Soudha demanding Minister B. Nagendra's resignation over the 2024 Valmiki ST welfare corporation scam, forcing past a security cordon; JD(S) joined. Nagendra refused to resign, calling it caste-based targeting, and said he'd answer on the Assembly floor. CM Shivakumar challenged the Opposition to file a formal debate notice. When Minister Muniyappa separately moved a resolution condemning a ritual after Congress chief Kharge's Haldwani rally, Ashoka withheld support unless Nagendra was sacked first — so it was dropped. The Assembly still passed 3 bills (including the Apartment Ownership Bill above) without discussion. Why it matters to you: a case study in how ministers accused of financial impropriety over discretionary government money get protected by coalition-math — recognise the same playbook wherever a state institution controls large discretionary funds or land allotments.
entries.src: Sources: Deccan Chronicle, ANI (10:36 AM IST), Deccan Herald & The News Minute · published 21 Aug 2026

entries.t: Frozen out of their own homes: hundreds converge on Telangana Bhavan as BRS opens a free legal cell for Section 22A victims
entries.s: Hundreds of Hyderabad-area owners whose land got wrongly frozen under the Section 22A “prohibited list” gathered at BRS headquarters seeking help. One case cited: Rajesh, HMT Housing Colony — bought his house on a bank loan in 2017, tried to sell it in 2026 after losing his job, and only discovered at registration that his survey number had been listed, despite the layout being HMDA-approved back in 1995. BRS announced a 10-lawyer free legal cell, led by advocate Kalyan, based at Telangana Bhavan. Why it matters to you: a plot can carry a clean sale deed, an approved layout, and 20+ years of tax receipts — and still freeze overnight if its survey number gets swept into 22A by a records-migration error. Check the live list before signing any JD, not just at diligence.

entries.t: Hyderabad’s outer bypass stalls again: NHAI pushes Regional Ring Road North bid deadline to today — a sixth delay
entries.s: NHAI has extended the construction-bid deadline for the ₹8,500+ crore, 161-km Sangareddy–Choutuppal stretch (NH161AA, the RRR’s northern half) for the sixth time since the tender first opened in November 2025 — this time to today. Reported causes: pending Central alignment approvals, and the state pushing for the northern and southern packages to be executed together. Why it matters to you: land near a confirmed ring-road alignment re-rates sharply once acquisition and construction actually lock in — but every extension pushes that trigger further out, which matters for holding-period math on any land bank along the corridor.

entries.t: Harish Rao writes to Rahul Gandhi demanding the Revenue Minister’s removal; Ponguleti hits back: “like a murderer expressing condolences”
entries.s: BRS deputy floor leader T. Harish Rao’s open letter to LoP Rahul Gandhi demands Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy’s dismissal, a judicial probe by a retired High Court judge, and a forensic audit of every 22A addition/removal since December 2023 — alleging a “30% commission” racket to get names off the list. Ponguleti hit back that BRS has “failed as the Opposition” and is “spreading falsehoods,” pointing to Dharani-era record flaws from the BRS government’s own tenure. Why it matters to you: if the forensic-audit demand ever succeeds, every 22A addition and removal since December 2023 becomes public record — the single best outcome for anyone buying land in the affected districts.

entries.t: Minister’s daughter accuses CM Revanth of a ₹200-crore land favour to his brother; Congress serves a showcause notice on her mother
entries.s: After CM Revanth Reddy publicly endorsed the sitting Parkal MLA for renomination — blindsiding Minister Konda Surekha’s camp, which had been positioning daughter Konda Sushmita for the ticket — Sushmita called the government a “TDP Congress,” called the CM “arrogant,” and revived a land-allotment allegation: 5 acres at Raviryal handed to a company for ₹7 crore against an estimated ₹200-crore market value, benefiting the CM’s brother. Congress’s disciplinary committee gave Surekha 3 days to explain her daughter’s remarks; she submitted her reply the same evening. Why it matters to you: a ₹200-crore-vs-₹7-crore government land allotment involving the sitting CM’s own family is a live case study in the gap between allotment price and market price on discretionary government land — the exact gap worth checking before touching any government-linked parcel.

entries.t: CM Revanth calls delimitation “anti-South India” at Congress’s top body, then leaves for a 10-day UK–US investment tour
entries.s: At Wednesday’s CWC meeting in Delhi, Revanth warned that a uniform 50% Lok Sabha seat increase would let bigger, faster-growing northern states decide who forms the central government, and pushed weighting seats by economic contribution instead. He then left today for Oxford, Cambridge and London Business School, then Boston, through 30 August, pitching Telangana for education and investment tie-ups — sending Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka to represent the state at the Southern Zonal Council instead (full story in Karnataka Politics below).

entries.t: PSU telecom firm ITI puts 44 acres of prime K.R. Puram land up for e-auction at a ₹1,685-crore reserve price
entries.s: The National Land Monetization Corporation has invited e-auction bids for ITI Limited’s 44.03-acre, commercially-zoned, vacant parcel on Old Madras Road/NH-75 in Krishnarajapuram — a ₹38.28-crore-per-acre reserve, about 12% below ITI’s own July sale of a nearby 21-acre piece at ₹43.5 crore/acre. It’s one piece of a ₹13,500-crore national drive to monetise BSNL/MTNL/RINL-linked land; technical bids and EMD are due 16 September. Why it matters to you: a concrete, dated benchmark — ₹38–43 crore/acre for vacant, commercially-zoned, highway-facing land in an established IT corridor — worth keeping in your back pocket when discussing land-value trajectories with JD partners along Hyderabad’s own IT-corridor belts.

entries.t: Karnataka’s Assembly stuck for a fourth straight day as the Opposition demands a minister’s resignation over a welfare-fund scam
entries.s: BJP and JD(S) disrupted the Karnataka Assembly for a fourth consecutive day, demanding Planning Minister B. Nagendra’s removal over 2024 embezzlement allegations at the Valmiki ST welfare corporation — he was reinducted into the cabinet on 3 August. LoP R. Ashoka displayed what he called a CBI chargesheet and claimed 24 pending cases; the Speaker adjourned the House for an hour. Nagendra calls it caste-based targeting and counters that 126 BJP ministers nationally carry criminal cases.

entries.t: Shivakumar tells the Centre: give the South its fair share of funds — and back Bengaluru’s Mekedatu water project
entries.s: At the 31st Southern Zonal Council, Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar told Union Home Minister Amit Shah that Karnataka’s Finance Commission tax share fell from 4.7% to 3.6% — a claimed ₹65,000-crore loss over six years — despite the state holding 5.5% of India’s population but generating ~9% of GDP and 42% of software exports. He defended the long-stalled Mekedatu dam as securing Bengaluru’s drinking water, raised the Upper Bhadra irrigation project, and asked the Centre to reconsider the new Mines and Minerals Act. Why it matters to you: Mekedatu’s fate is a leading indicator for Bengaluru’s long-term water security — the same “where’s the water coming from” question worth asking of any long-horizon Hyderabad land bet.

school.t: Pahani & RoR 1-B — the complete masterclass
school.s: Everything about Telangana's two core revenue records, from Salar Jung's surveyors to the Bhu Bharati Act — every column, every court ruling, every fraud pattern, with worked examples throughout. The deep-research edition.

school.t: Pahani & RoR 1-B: Telangana’s two core revenue records
school.s: Most buyers ask for the sale deed. Smart buyers ask for the Pahani and RoR 1-B first — what the land IS, and who it BELONGS to, straight from the Tahsildar's register.

school.t: Pattadar Passbook: Telangana’s Aadhaar-linked title document
school.s: The sale deed registers the transaction; the Passbook is what the revenue system recognises as ownership. Skip the transfer and the previous owner can legally re-mutate your land.

school.t: Adangal: the cultivation register that exposes what title records hide
school.s: RoR 1-B handles who owns; Adangal handles who FARMS — and its Land Nature column (Patta / Sarkari / Assigned) can end a deal in one word.

school.t: Title deed & Mother Deed (Mula Deed): tracing Telangana’s chain of title
school.s: One Mother Deed per property; many sale deeds branch from it. The 30-year search starts at the root — and IGRS only reaches back to 1983.

school.t: Bhu Bharati land details: reading the restored 11-column Pahani online
school.s: Dharani thinned the record; Bhu Bharati brought the columns back. The enjoyment column — who actually occupies the land — is the one that costs lakhs when ignored.

school.t: Certified Pahani copy: the digitally signed PDF that banks actually accept
school.s: A screenshot can be edited in minutes; the signed PDF is cryptographically tied to the record. QR + Tahsildar signature + Bhudhaar — or it doesn't count.

school.t: Searching Telangana land records by name
school.s: A discovery tool, not proof: locate inherited or undocumented holdings by pattadar name — then confirm every hit with father's name, extent and LPM before trusting it.

school.t: Bhu Naksha: Telangana’s cadastral map, rebuilt by drones
school.s: The visual half of your land record — the 2025 drone resurvey rebuilt every boundary from the air, and the GPS-anchored LPM map now outranks the old paper sketch in boundary fights.

school.t: The Bhudhaar number: one parcel, one ID
school.s: Telangana's unique land-parcel ID, bound to GPS-mapped boundaries. Permanent status is the gate registration itself keys on — making it the cheapest fraud filter in the state.

school.t: The LPM number: mapping old survey numbers to the drone resurvey
school.s: Survey numbers were descriptions; LPMs are coordinates. Your deed speaks the old language, the live record speaks the new — diligence means carrying both, plus the Bhudhaar.

school.t: Know Your Position: the GPS check that kills the two-fields-over trick
school.s: Stand on the land, and the phone shows which parcel polygon you're inside. Orientation, not adjudication — but no document closes the shown-vs-documented gap like it.

school.t: Auto-mutation: when the system updates the Pahani for you — and when it doesn’t
school.s: Registration is supposed to trigger mutation automatically within ~7 days. When sync fails — and it has, thousands of times — the gap is an open door for the old owner. Here's the escalation path.

school.t: Mutation on Bhu Bharati: the auto path for sales, the Tahsildar path for inheritance
school.s: Sale mutation runs itself IF the identifiers were right; inheritance always needs a filing. Either way the finish line is the same: Pahani in the new name, passbook to match.

school.t: Legal Heir Certificate (Family Member Certificate): who inherits, on paper
school.s: The MRO's list of every legal successor — the document mutation and pensions run on. The most common defect: married daughters left off, which Vineeta Sharma (2020) makes fatal to any later sale.

school.t: RoR correction: one year to fix the record — closing 13 April 2026
school.s: The Act's bargain: one clean year to repair Dharani-era errors, after which entries attain FINALITY. Name, extent, survey linkage, classification — paper wins these cases.

school.t: The Encumbrance Certificate in Telangana: Form 15, Form 16, and what neither shows
school.s: Every registered transaction on the parcel — sales, mortgages, gifts, attachments. But a Nil EC is not automatically clean, 1983 is the digital floor, and the Pahani's liabilities column sees what the EC can't.

school.t: EC on IGRS: the right portal, the right period, the right reading
school.s: EC and market value live on IGRS — NOT Bhu Bharati; that single confusion tops the new system's help desks. Document-number search, 30-year windows, and entry-type literacy.

school.t: The 22A prohibited-land check: two portals, one clause, dated screenshots
school.s: Six categories the SRO must refuse — and a list that has wrongly swallowed thousands of genuine patta parcels (one crore acres under review). Check both portals, read the CLAUSE, screenshot with the date.

school.t: The 22A list on IGRS: category by category, cure by cure
school.s: Government, assigned, endowment, wakf, court-attached — each category fails a purchase differently, and partial listings mean the check runs on the exact survey number, not the village.

school.t: Registration slot booking: where all your diligence gets consumed
school.s: The slot opens only against a verified permanent Bhudhaar — so booking problems are usually identifier problems in disguise. Challan maths, party attendance, and the exam-day framing.

school.t: Government market value by survey number: the state’s price beneath your price
school.s: Duty runs on the higher of the government's basic value and your deal price — no arbitrage in under-declaring, only exposure. And the value lives on IGRS, not Bhu Bharati.

school.t: Tracking Bhu Bharati applications: the acknowledgment number is the case
school.s: Files move for applicants who watch them. The stage ladder, the weekly-screenshot habit, and the rule that no final payment moves while a seller's promised filing still reads 'submitted'.

school.t: Can I buy land in Telangana? Rules, ceilings, and the benami line
school.s: Open to every Indian citizen — no farmer test, no state-origin bar, all 33 districts. The real limits: ceiling caps, the 22-A list, and the benami trap that confiscates.

school.t: HMDA & DTCP layout approval: the LP number, the right portal, and the mortgage-plot check
school.s: HMDA approves inside the metro region, DTCP everywhere else — same LP number logic, different portals. Plus the check most buyers miss: whether YOUR plot is one HMDA holds as mortgage security.

school.t: HMDA Development Permission: tentative LP, final LP, and the 15% mortgage
school.s: The two-stage sanction that turns raw metro-region land into a marketable layout — AI scrutiny, ground inspection, and the mortgaged 15% that releases only when the roads are real.

school.t: Building plan approval on BuildNow: the sanctioned plan, deemed approval, and the demolition task force
school.s: AI scrutiny in minutes, deemed approval in 21 days, ₹1 tokens — and a District Collector task force that demolishes unauthorised buildings WITHOUT notice. Telangana's carrot-and-stick in one permit.

school.t: NALA conversion (the Act & the process): from farmland classification to buildable land
school.s: Agricultural classification is a permission, not a description. The 2006 Act's route: apply, public notice, pay the tax, get the order — and the 'deemed conversion' trap that fines you 50% extra for building first.

school.t: NALA on Bhu Bharati: the integrated flow, and what changes after the order
school.s: The application, the record and the classification now live in one system — faster, but with sync quirks. The before/after table every plot buyer should know by heart.

school.t: Property tax receipts & the PTIN: the small document that gates mutation
school.s: Ten digits, half-yearly cycles, 2% monthly interest on arrears — and Section 208's rule that mutation waits until every paisa clears. The receipt is small; its leverage is not.

school.t: Bhu Bharati: the portal that now runs Telangana’s land records — a map of every service
school.s: The 2025 system that replaced Dharani: what lives where, which service answers which question, and the order to use them in. Start every Telangana land journey on this page.

school.t: The Sale Deed: what it is, how registration works, and why it matters
school.s: Paying for land does not make it yours. Possession does not make it yours. One registered document does — and everything else is just a promise.

school.t: Power of attorney for property: why a GPA sale is risky
school.s: A Power of Attorney lets someone act for the owner. It never makes anyone the owner — and the Supreme Court has said so twice.

school.t: How to check land disputes and litigation before buying
school.s: A clean-looking deed says nothing about the court case attached to the land. Here is the full drill for finding the fights the seller will not mention.

school.t: RERA for plotted developments: what plot buyers must verify
school.s: Cross a size threshold and a plot venture needs RERA registration like any apartment tower. 'RERA approved' on a hoarding means nothing.

school.t: ULPIN: what the 'Aadhaar for land' means for buyers
school.s: India is giving every surveyed parcel a 14-digit ID tied to its map coordinates — the same trick Aadhaar played on duplicate identities, now aimed at land fraud.

school.t: Encumbrance Certificate: what it shows, what it misses, and why it matters
school.s: The EC is the first document every lawyer pulls — and the most misunderstood. It is a transaction history, not a certificate of ownership.

school.t: Property title search: what it is, how it works, and why it matters
school.s: A sale deed proves a transaction happened. A title search proves the whole chain behind it was clean — thirty years of it.

school.t: Lal Dora and Abadi Deh land: what buyers should know before investing
school.s: Inside the old village habitation line, land often grew without building permissions or clear titles — cheap, central, and legally a different world.

school.t: Agricultural land ceiling limits by state: how much you can own
school.s: Post-independence laws still cap agricultural holdings — with limits that change by state and by how well-watered the acre is.

school.t: Converting agricultural land to non-agricultural (NA) use: the complete guide
school.s: Every parcel in India is agricultural by default. Building anything on it first needs a formal change of land use — the NA order.

school.t: How to calculate land value from the DLC / circle rate
school.s: Rate per unit × area = the government's minimum value for your land. Simple maths, several traps.

school.t: Circle rate vs market value vs guidance value: what decides stamp duty
school.s: Every parcel carries two prices — the government's and the market's. Stamp duty always follows the higher one, and a big gap can bite both sides at tax time.

school.t: NRI buying land in India: rules and repatriation
school.s: NRIs buy houses and offices freely — farmland is essentially barred. And the account the money came FROM decides how much can ever go back.

school.t: Buying farm land near a city: an investment guide
school.s: Peri-urban farmland is really a bet on the city's growth, not on crops. Priced that way, it can be excellent — sold as farm income, it is usually a trap.

school.t: How to sell your land online in India: process and paperwork
school.s: A listing finds the buyer; the law still runs the transfer. Verification, agreement, deed, duty, registration — then the mutation everyone forgets.

school.t: How to buy agricultural land in India: rules, verification, and costs
school.s: Who may buy is state law; what to verify is universal; and the sticker price is never the full price.

school.t: Land acquisition by government: compensation rules under the RFCTLARR Act
school.s: Acquisition is not a negotiation — but the payout follows a formula worth knowing: market value × location multiplier + 100% solatium, plus rehabilitation.

school.t: Joint Development Agreement: how builder and owner shares work
school.s: Land from one side, construction money from the other, and a ratio in between — the structure that builds most of urban India, and Vivek's core trade.

school.t: Bank loans for agricultural land: eligibility, documents, and how to apply
school.s: Banks do lend against farmland — term loans at 70–85% of value — and their checklist is a free second opinion on your title.

school.t: NRI guide to buying land in India: rules, restrictions, and what to know
school.s: Flats and offices: freely. Farmland: banned under FEMA, with three narrow doors. And absentee buying makes every ordinary check twice as important.

school.t: Common land scams in India and how to protect yourself
school.s: Seven repeatable frauds — forged titles, restricted land, double sales, PoA abuse, encroachment, benami deals, fake pre-launches — and the checks that defeat each one.

school.t: Assigned land: why it cannot be sold and what the law says
school.s: Government-granted land to the landless poor carries a permanent transfer ban. A registered deed on it is worth nothing — and the buyer can face jail.

school.t: CRZ rules: how far from the coast you can build
school.s: Four zones from mangrove to open sea decide whether coastal land is buildable at all — and the famous 50-metre relaxation only switches on when the state's coastal plan is approved.

school.t: How to resolve land boundary disputes using survey records
school.s: Cadastral maps and Field Measurement Books outrank memories and old fences. The playbook: records → official survey → talk → notice → court. And delay can literally lose the land.

school.t: Power of Attorney for land: rules, risks, and what holds up in court
school.s: A PoA lets someone act for you — it never transfers ownership, however grand the wording. The Supreme Court closed that door in 2011 and bolted it in 2023.

school.t: How to convert agricultural land to residential property
school.s: The sequence is everything: master plan zone first, application second, fee last. And a conversion order is a conditional, time-bound document — not a permanent status.

school.t: Mutation of land records: what it is and why it matters
school.s: Registration transfers ownership; mutation tells the government about it. Skip it and the tax bills, loan rejections and resale objections arrive years later.

school.t: How to transfer land ownership after the owner’s death
school.s: Title never moves on its own — someone must file. Wills, personal succession law, heir certificates, and the December 2025 change that ended mandatory probate.

school.t: Capital gains tax on agricultural land sale
school.s: Rural farmland is not a capital asset at all — zero capital gains tax. The test is mechanical: census population and aerial kilometres. Urban farmland is taxed, with 54B and 54EC as the exits.

school.t: How to calculate stamp duty and registration charges on land
school.s: Two separate levies at the SRO — the state's transfer tax and the recording fee — computed on the higher of price and guideline value, with state-by-state rates and concessions.

school.t: Guideline value vs market value: what every land buyer should know
school.s: The state's benchmark sets the floor for duty and tax; the market sets the price. The gap between the two decides duty, TDS thresholds — and a tax trap under Section 56(2)(x).

school.t: DTCP approval explained: what it means for plot buyers
school.s: The layout permit that certifies roads, open space and zoning — never title. The verification is one thing only: the LP number, searched by YOU on the official portal.

school.t: The real difference between patta, sale deed, and title deed
school.s: A tax record, a transfer instrument, and a category term — three things buyers conflate. Only the registered deed moves ownership; the patta only supports it.

school.t: How to check if a plot is legally safe to buy
school.s: No builder, bank or RERA badge is checking a plot for you — verification is entirely the buyer's job. The full drill: chain, EC, court search, records, zoning, survey.

school.t: UDR patta vs regular patta: what “updating of registry” means for your title
school.s: The 1980s computerisation of Tamil Nadu's revenue records — what it changed, the errors it created (mismatches in 61% of sampled villages), and why banks now expect the digital record.

school.t: 2C patta explained: why assigned land drags buyers into CID cases
school.s: Welfare-assigned land carries restrictions that survive every later deed — and buying it can mean criminal charges, not just a void sale. Also: why 2C patta and assigned patta are NOT the same thing.

school.t: Raidurg’s ₹237 crore acre: madness, or underpriced?
school.s: 1acre's case study in reading a headline price like a developer: FSI maths turns ₹237 Cr/acre into ₹5,500 per buildable sq ft — and the GCC demand engine explains the rest.
